page: Amazon Web Services m7a.12xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose compute instance powered by AMD EPYC 9R14 processors running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance provides 48 dedicated physical cores with 48 vCPUs operating at 3.7 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 192.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM at 5 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 19 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and supports instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. It includes no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, relying entirely on remote Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent disk operations.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational and memory performance. The 48 dedicated AMD cores achieve top-tier multi-core throughput in stress-ng tests, ranking in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, alongside strong single-core execution in the top 25 percent. DDR5 memory throughput is notable, posting 196.87 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 124.3 GB/sec for uncached writes. Application-level evaluations show high throughput, including 115.33 million Redis SET operations per second, 50,421.0 in Clang compilation, and 45.84 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-bound machine learning tasks also display strong efficiency in quantized prompt processing and medium-parameter text generation.

From an infrastructure perspective, the dedicated 1-to-1 core mapping avoids hyperthread contention, resulting in consistent runtime performance under sustained multi-threaded execution. The absence of local NVMe storage requires careful consideration of EBS network bandwidth allocation for I/O-heavy pipelines. Considering its large DDR5 memory footprint and high parallel throughput, the m7a.12xlarge provides strong resource density and cost efficiency for large backend web servers, enterprise database engines, CI/CD compilation farms, and distributed data processing frameworks.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.12xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by 48 dedicated physical cores of AMD EPYC 9R14 processors running at 3.7 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Configured with a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the instance provides 192.0 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 memory and 19 Gbps of baseline networking. It contains no attached GPUs or local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached EBS for persistence. Benchmark metrics place its multi-core CPU performance in the top 10 percent, complemented by strong memory bandwidth and top-quartile results in compilation, Redis transaction rates, and web serving. Because it allocates dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, it delivers predictable performance free from thread contention. The instance is well suited for demanding application backends, memory-intensive distributed caching, software build pipelines, and enterprise relational database engines.
